content.text: : complex clinical syndrome that results from any structural or functional impairment of ventricular filling or ejection of blood leading to cardinal manifestations of dyspnea, fatigue, fluid retention
: leading cause of hospitalization in US
MC 2/2 L-sided HF or pulm dz
: pts w/ longstanding (e.g., months-years) s/sxs of HF
: rapid onset or worsening of sxs of HF; most episodes result from worsening of chronic HF, but ~20% are due to new-onset HF that can occur in the setting of
ACS, acute valvular dysfunction, hypertensive urgency, postcardiotomy syndrome
•chronic pulmonary vascular disease (cor pulmonale, pulmonary arterial HTN)
: thyrotoxicosis, obesity, anemia, cirrhosis, AV shunt, chronic lung disease, vitamin B deficiency (beriberi), myeloproliferative disorder
: elevated cardiac filling pressure &/or inadequate peripheral oxygen delivery, at rest or during stress, caused by cardiac dysfunction
▪︎LHF can → RHF = biventricular failure (signs + sxs of both)
•apical impulse displaced downward & to the Lt
▪︎S3 gallop = systolic HF; S4 gallop = diastolic HF (S3 may be nl <30yo)
: anxious, diaphoretic, dyspneic, pallor, duskiness, cool extremities, cyanosis
▪︎low CO → poor perfusion (altered mentation, cool extremities, hypotension, narrow pulse pressure) → sus cardiogenic shock
= severe dz + arrest may be imminent (assess end-organ perfusion)
▪︎tachypnea, tachy, & HTN common; ± accessory muscle use
: ⍉limitation of activity, ordinary activity does ⍉cause Sx
: slight limitation; comfortable @ rest, but ordinary activity → Sx
: marked limitation; only comfortable @ rest, < ordinary activity → Sx
: Sx @ rest, unable to carry out any activity w.o Sx
: sus if 1+ s/sxs of HF w/ ⍉apparent ⍉cardiac cause
diastol dysfun, LVH, valve stenosis or regurg, LA enlrg, ↑pulm a. systol P
▪︎bedside echo if cardiac or valvular fxn ⍉known
▪︎BNP/NT-proBNP ⇡ in HF exacerbations, but other conditions can ⇡natriuretic peptides too
(AHA: >400 = rule-in; ≥100 = sensitive rule-out in acute dyspnea; 100-400 = gray zone)
▪︎BNP = cardiomyocyte wall stress, ⍉direct measure of total body fluid → supports, ⍉proves, congestion
▪︎BNP/NT-proBNP ⇡ in HF but low specificity + sensitivity
▪︎BNP distinguishes CHF vs dyspnea of pulm etiology
, LA enlrg, LVH, pathologic Q waves
▪︎nl ECG in HF w/ LV dysfxn is rare
▪︎CXR helps distinguish HF from pulm dz
: RHC w/ PCWP assessed @ rest & w/ exercise
: smoke cessation, EToH restriction, sodium ≤3g/d, fluid ≤1.5-2L/d, wt loss, cardiac rehab
– weigh daily to detect fluid accumulation
▪︎2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA: primary pharm therapy for HFrEF = RAAS antagonist + BB + MRA + SGLT2i
▪︎the 3 proven BBs ⇣mortality + improve Sx in all HFrEF; generally add before MRA when starting
▪︎relieve Sx + signs of vol overload; ⍉shown to ⇣mortality
: for pts that cannot take ARNI or ACEI (“sartan”)
: alt to angiotensin blockers (ARNI, ACEI, ARB)
▪︎Black pts w/ NYHA III-IV HFrEF on GDMT: ⇣mortality
•MRA (spironolactone, eplerenone): NYHA class II-IV HF if GFR >30 + K <5
Other 2/2 therapies depend on Clin Use
▪︎SGLT2i prevent hospitalization in HFrEF w/ T2DM + established/high CV risk
▪︎advanced HF: mechanical assist device, ICD, heart transplant
▪︎statins ⍉beneficial as adjunctive tx for HF alone
▪︎chronic HF + AFib + additional stroke RF → chronic AC
▪︎routine combined ACEI + ARB + MRA = potentially harmful
▪︎amlodipine = only CCB w/ established safety in pts w/ severe HF
: first line for vol overload w/ congestion (IV w/o delay; ↑doses if on chronic diuretics or kidney dz)
: used for pulm congestion for rapid relief of dyspnea
: 2nd-line vasodilator in acute HF; unpredictable, prolonged BP-lowering
: sit pt up, have legs dangle over bed to decrease preload/venous return; (+) P (ventilation)
▪︎⍉BBs in ADHF (⍉start BBs; ⍉IV BBs in decompensated/unstable HF)
▪︎O2 if SpO2 <90%; monitor O2 sat/vitals/rhythm; 2 IVs; pt upright
▪︎NIV PRN (⍉if immediate intubation needed or NIV CI)
▪︎search cause: AF w/ RVR → slow HR; new-onset AF + instability or refractory Sx → DCC; acute MR/AR or ascending aortic dissection → immediate cardiac surg consult
▪︎adequate perfusion + fluid overload → early vasodilator; ⇣preload if diuretic response ⍉adequate
▪︎systol HF + cardiogenic shock: d/c chronic BB; IV inotrope ± mechanical support
▪︎diastol HF + shock: possible LV outflow obstruction → BB, IV fluid (unless pulm edema), IV vasopressor; ⍉inotrope or vasodilator; immediate echo
▪︎hypotension w/o shock → dobutamine (may worsen hypotension); severe hypotension + shock → norepinephrine
▪︎IV iron (ferric carboxymaltose): ⇡functional outcomes in HF + iron deficiency
▪︎compression stockings: ⇡venous return → useful for dependent LE edema
